facts.fact: UNDP's IDT4M annual report states that in 2025 the Nzika mobile application was rolled out for registration of National ID, community births, community deaths and marriages by registration officers at Traditional Authority offices.

The report describes Nzika as a unified platform integrating National ID, birth, death and marriage registration, used by registration officers on mobile kits in communities with biometric authentication and offline working, giving what it calls real-time services integrated with the national CRVS system; it does not describe the synchronisation step.

UNDP reports that NRB rolled out registration on the Nzika app at 87 service points in five districts in 2025 (Balaka 21, Karonga 12, Lilongwe 22, Mchinji 28, Mwanza 4); its results framework gives 87 functional NRB field offices providing continuous ID and civil registration against a 2025 target of 150, and 5 districts with a functional integrated system against a target of 10. The report's table of the NRB Strategic Plan lists 277 Traditional Authorities and 138 Sub-TAs in 28 districts for expansion by 2030.

The report dates the rollout of Nzika registration at 87 service points in five districts to 2025, with registrations recorded in the last quarter of 2025, and calls it a move from piloting to scaling; national rollout is a plan for 2026.
The report states that the National Registration Bureau rolled out and operates Nzika registration with its own registration officers and ICT staff, with technical and financial support from UNDP.

The report states that the NRB Strategic Plan 2025-2030 was launched in 2025 and provides for expanding NRB services to Traditional Authority and Sub-TA level by 2030, and that national rollout of the integrated Nzika system is planned for 2026.

The report states that the Nzika rollout had UNDP's technical and financial support under the IDT4M basket fund, which spent USD 2,107,228 on its digital ID and CRVS output in 2025; it names no domestic budget line for the system.

UNDP reports 104,177 births registered in 2025 through continuous registration embedded in health services, with 56,268 certificates issued at the point of care in maternity wards; the same report elsewhere gives over 575,000 births registered in 2025.

UNDP reports that integrated digital printers were deployed to 58 health facilities in 2025, where NRB civil registration at the maternity ward issues the birth certificate before the mother leaves; no total of facilities is given.
UNDP reports 19,125 deaths registered in 2025 and 2,048 death certificates issued, with the integrated system automatically matching death records to National ID numbers.
